history: The daily drink of Martinique and Guadeloupe. The custom is chacun prépare sa propre mort—each prepares their own death—so the bottle goes on the table and the guest builds it.
whyItWorks: Agricole is pressed from fresh cane juice, not molasses; it tastes grassy and raw, and this build exists to show that off rather than cover it.
steps: Cut a coin-sized disc from the side of a lime, taking peel and a little flesh.
Muddle it gently with the cane syrup in the glass—press, do not pulverize.
Add the rhum and stir. Serve at room temperature, or over a single cube.
techniqueNotes: Serving it neat is the tradition; a single large cube is the common concession.
Do not use lime juice. The oil in the peel is most of the point.

substitutions.notes: Cane syrup is thicker and more molasses-forward; simple works at ⅓ oz.
A molasses rum makes a decent drink and a bad Ti’ Punch.

name: Ti' Punch
description: Rhum agricole, cane syrup, a disc of lime. No ice, no shaking, no apology.
